briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Bills Stack Up in Lansing While a National Cannabis M&A Wave and Psychedelics Progress Build Momentum
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax keeps drawing bipartisan fire — with a new House repeal bill and the GOP governor nominee both promising relief — giving operators a real political path forward even as sales stay soft. Nationally, Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis and a fresh DEA procedural milestone show rescheduling-fueled deal-making and momentum are very much alive.

local.text: State Rep. filed HB 6224 on July 29 to fully repeal the 24% wholesale marijuana tax, joining a bipartisan Senate repeal bill — a second legislative track now pushing to unwind the levy that funds road repairs.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a platform promising to repeal or sharply cut the wholesale tax while cracking down on unregulated hemp THC and illicit grows — putting cannabis tax relief front-and-center in the November race.

Democratic candidate Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson has also pledged to repeal the tax if elected, arguing the state 'cannot balance state budgets on the backs of one industry' — meaning whoever wins in November, operators have a friendly ear on this issue.

C3 Industries opened a new High Profile Cannabis dispensary in Luna Pier, expanding retail reach along the Michigan-Ohio border near Toledo as part of its continued strategic retail growth in high-demand markets.

Recreational sales fell to $1.48 billion in the first half of 2026, but MDOT's own financial plan still bakes in $315 million from the wholesale tax this fiscal year — while flagging it remains subject to constitutional litigation that could reshape those numbers entirely.
local.source: Detroit Metro Times / The Marijuana Herald

national.text: Curaleaf formally launched a hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis on Aug. 18, offering $4/share (up to $5) in a deal valuing Aurora near $260 million and aiming to build 'the preeminent, scaled industry leader' spanning 17 countries.

The DEA's cannabis rescheduling process cleared a key procedural milestone on Aug. 18, keeping the move from Schedule I to Schedule III on track, with an NPRM expected before year-end and a final rule possibly landing in 2027.

The DEA released the full 2,533-page transcript of its marijuana rescheduling hearing as Chief ALJ Derek Julius prepares his recommendation, with the agency arguing in its final brief that cannabis 'no longer fits the statutory requirements for Schedule I.'

Compass Pathways is now working with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs on a randomized controlled trial testing COMP360 psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression and PTSD in veterans, donating the study drug for the multi-site PIVOT trial.

Green Thumb Industries enters the post-rescheduling landscape from a position of strength — grew revenue and earnings last quarter and stands to retain significantly more operating cash flow once Section 280E penalties are eliminated, fueling speculation it could join the acquisition wave.
